key_insight: An AI-agent-assisted, Lean-verified pipeline checks whether a quantum device’s low-energy states preserve the intended topological code space despite unwanted interactions.
engineering_relevance: The workflow guides device tuning by identifying dominant unwanted couplings and testing parameters against a prescribed leakage budget.
method: Construct the ideal code Hamiltonian and determine its protective excitation gap.
Compare unwanted energy-shift bounds from interaction-strength sums, anticommuting Pauli grouping, and diagonalization.
Use an AI agent to find viable device parameters and Lean to verify low-energy isolation and code-space agreement.
evidence_signal: In an eight-qubit toric-code superconducting device model, Lean verifies four isolated low-energy states close to the ideal code space, while Pauli grouping gives tighter bounds than interaction-strength sums.
watch_item: The demonstration concerns an eight-qubit device model; experimental robustness and scalability to larger codes remain to be established.
paper_title: Agentic Pipelines for Mapping Topological Codes to Quantum Hardware
